# Jyovika Aswale: Analytics Portfolio

This repository contains a curated collection of data analysis projects written in R and published through Quarto. Each project focuses on clear statistical reasoning, polished visualisation, and insights that connect data to real decision making.

I use this portfolio to demonstrate my approach to analysis:

  - Start with exploration, understand how the data behaves, choose suitable models, test assumptions, communicate uncertainty, and present results in a way that anyone can understand.

## 🔍 What You Will Find Here

#### Data Analysis and Modelling

  - Causal inference: difference-in-differences, fixed effects and event studies
  - Distribution fitting
  - Simulation and bootstrapping
  - Regression and sensitivity analysis
  - Hypothesis testing and confidence interval estimation
  - Exploratory data analysis with tidy workflows

#### Visualisation and Communication
  - ggplot2 graphics designed for clarity
  - Diagnostic plots that show how models behave
  - Story driven blog posts published through Quarto
  - Layouts and themes created with custom CSS
  
#### Reproducible Workflows
  - Each project is built in Quarto
  - Code, data, and results stay together
  - The repository contains all supporting scripts and assets needed to rebuild the site

## 📂 Featured Projects

#### 1. Do Fast Pit Stops Win F1 Races or Is It Just Hype?

An R powered exploration of Formula 1 data

- Skills: correlation, regression, bootstrapping, data wrangling

- Highlights:

  - Cleaning and transforming multi season F1 datasets
  
  - Measuring the impact of a single second lost in the pit lane
  
  - Sensitivity analysis to compare team performance
  
  - Custom colour palettes and visual styling
  
- Blog: [read it on my website](https://jyovika.github.io/jyovika-analytics-portfolio/posts/f1/f1.html)

#### 2. How Busy Are Melbourne’s CBD Crossings?

A statistical deep dive into pedestrian flow

- Skills: distribution fitting, bootstrapping, model diagnostics, visualisation

- Highlights:

  - Normal, Lognormal, and Gamma modelling
  
  - Bootstrap simulation for percentile estimation
  
  - Engineering style decision analysis based on traffic thresholds
  
  - Revenue estimation using binomial proportion confidence intervals
  
- Blog: [read it on my website](https://jyovika.github.io/jyovika-analytics-portfolio/posts/pedestrian/pedestrian.html)

#### 3. Did Closing Police Station Counters Increase Crime in Victoria?

A causal analysis of Victoria Police's 2023-24 reception hour cuts

- Skills: difference-in-differences, fixed effects regression, event studies, Poisson models

- Highlights:

  - Panel of recorded crime for all 79 Victorian local government areas, 2017 to 2026
  
  - Treatment group built by mapping 43 stations with reduced hours to their local government areas
  
  - Event-study check of the parallel trends assumption, reported honestly where it is imperfect
  
  - Separate estimates by offence type, with burglary the only clear change
  
- Blog: [read it on my website](https://jyovika.github.io/jyovika-analytics-portfolio/posts/police_closure/police_station_closure.html)

## 🎨 Custom Styling

## 🔧 How to Build Locally

If you want to render the full site:

Install [Quarto](https://quarto.org) and these R packages:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "MASS", "boot", "broom", "here", "rsample",
                   "scales", "readxl", "fixest", "kableExtra", "knitr"))
```

Then, from the project folder:

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
quarto render
```

The site is written to `docs/`, which GitHub Pages serves directly, so commit the updated `docs/` along with your changes.
